A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACMap and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite substantial appendix rearrangement.

before.justification: v1 reports original ACMap accuracy, inference-time measurements, component ablations and prototype-alignment analyses across five benchmarks.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds balanced-VTAB experiments, broader comparisons and additional prototype-alignment and stopping diagnostics.

M1.justification: The adapter architecture, weight averaging, initial weight replacement, centroid mapping and early-stopping procedure remain unchanged. Appendix D adds guidance for choosing the existing stopping threshold, without specifying a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, CUB, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A and the same five VTAB subsets for class-incremental learning. Balanced VTAB and the additional CIFAR task partition change sampling and evaluation settings within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with iCaRL, DER, FOSTER, MEMO, RanPAC and InfLoRA in Table B, timing comparisons with the four replay methods in Figure C, and semantic drift compensation (SDC) in Figure G. The original comparator sets remain. Correcting ADAM to APER in Section 5.2 is a naming correction; both versions' plots already show APER.

E3.justification: Supplementary evaluations introduce equal sample counts per VTAB task, CIFAR B0 Inc10 and a stated budget of 20 exemplars per class for replay baselines. The balanced sampling procedure is not fully specified. Existing main evaluation settings, accuracy metrics and Table A training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a controlled balanced-VTAB analysis testing the imbalance explanation, consecutive-adapter prototype similarities to guide early stopping, and a direct CM-versus-SDC alignment analysis. These materially expand validation of failure conditions and component behavior. The original ablations and loss-landscape analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both Appendix B versions specify five runs with seeds 1993-1997. v2 applies the existing averaging practice to additional results, including RanPAC, without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 retain identical numerical results, but v2 adds substantial comparative evidence. Table B reports final accuracies of 89.3 versus 91.5 for ACMap and RanPAC on CIFAR B0 Inc10, and 73.5 versus 77.4 on IN-R B0 Inc20. New plots report nearly coincident balanced-VTAB accuracy curves, better alignment for CM than SDC, and additional timing and stopping trends. These are added comparisons, not improvements to retained v1 scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, assumptions, Equations 1-7 and Algorithm 1 are retained. The new cosine-similarity diagnostics provide empirical evidence rather than new proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The third introductory contribution changes from claiming state-of-the-art accuracy and the fastest inference speed to performance comparable to the state of the art in both respects. The central claims about exemplar-free adapter consolidation, centroid mapping and constant inference cost otherwise remain.

C2.justification: v1 attributes VTAB weakness to both domain gaps and possible data imbalance. v2 removes the generalized domain-gap explanation and uses balanced-VTAB results to favor imbalance over an inherent ACMap limitation. It also adds an accumulated-error explanation for SDC and discusses resource tradeoffs for RanPAC and InfLoRA.

D1.justification: v2 adds qualitative guidance for selecting the stopping threshold, but removes v1's explicit pretrained-checkpoint URL while retaining the ViT-B/16 ImageNet-21K specification and general model-library link. Architecture details, Table A hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing and the ACMap code URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive positioning against iTAML, TKIL and RAPF, distinguishing replay requirements, merging costs and multimodal supervision. New references and appendix discussions cover RanPAC, InfLoRA and SDC, substantially broadening comparison with relevant prior approaches. Prompt-based related work is also expanded.

P1.justification: v2 makes mostly sentence-level edits, repairs malformed passages in related work and Appendix C, and corrects ADAM to APER. Appendix sections are reorganized and renamed, while the main section sequence and most existing exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table B and Figures C, D, F and G. Existing appendix accuracy and alignment plots are rearranged from three-by-three grids into narrower two-column arrangements; v1 Figures C and D become v2 Figures H and I. References change from two to three columns, and several main-text displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the previously speculative VTAB explanation, adds direct SDC and broader baseline comparisons, and repairs broken prose. These improve the paper's evidential value and readability. The gains are limited by sparse balanced-sampling details and broad accuracy claims that are not fully reconciled with RanPAC's higher Table B scores. Removing the exact checkpoint link also slightly reduces reproducibility information.
